$comment: Canonical InkExplain archetype registry. Edit this file, then run `npm run build:docs` to regenerate references/routing.md and the README archetype tables. Validated by `npm run validate`; see docs/adding-an-archetype.md.

archetypes.name: InkExplain Sketch
archetypes.summary: InkExplain's own brand-neutral style: black ink line art, one explainer-blue flow accent, a single highlighter-yellow emphasis, and a neutral ink figure or hands that perform the idea.

motionDna.actor: The ink figure, a pair of hands entering the frame, or the working object itself
poses: the whole body leans into the load
an arc of the body reaches across the gap the idea crosses
hands enter from the frame edge to place, hold, or adjust
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image; mini comics use two to four beats: setup, action, result

styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 by default on a clean white background, at least 35% empty
styleSheet.linework: Medium-thin black ink with a slight wobble, rounded ends, and sparse hatching
avoid: mascots, logos, and franchise characters
slides, infographics, and UI
textures, gradients, and shadows
3D or glossy vector art

sampleGates.decision: No rendered samples yet. InkExplain Sketch is original to InkExplain; publish renders after a quality review.

archetypes.name: Xiaohei
archetypes.summary: Ian's Xiaohei, a small solid-black creature with white dot eyes and thin legs, doing serious, slightly absurd work inside sparse black-ink sketches on a pure white page.

motionDna.actor: Xiaohei, the solid-black creature, as the serious operator inside the idea
poses: the whole black body leaning into a lever, a rope, or a press
thin legs braced under a load or mid-step along a path
white dot eyes fixed on the work, deadpan whatever happens
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image; mini comics use two or three beats with Xiaohei drawn the same way in every panel

styleSheet.medium: A sparse hand-drawn explainer sketch in black ink
styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 on a pure white page, at least 35% empty; the main subject fills about 40-60%
styleSheet.linework: Thin black hand-drawn lines with a slight wobble; never vector, mechanical, or heavy outlines
avoid: cute mascot, sticker, or children's-cartoon looks
commercial illustration, PPT infographics, and formal flowcharts
beige, textured, gradient, or shaded backgrounds
3D shading, glossy eyes, and costumes

legalNotice.credit: Xiaohei is the recurring character of Ian Xiaohei Illustrations by Ian (https://github.com/helloianneo/ian-xiaohei-illustrations), MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 Ian, inspected at commit 4102eb8
restrictions: Keep the Ian Xiaohei Illustrations name or credit Ian in any documentation derived from this archetype.
No claims that Ian created, endorses, or is affiliated with InkExplain or the generated images.

sampleGates.decision: Reviewed and approved for public gallery showcase with English and Chinese calibration sets.

archetypes.name: Littlebox
archetypes.summary: A closed paper-box character in thick rough marker on a pure white page that turns ideas into collecting, packaging, sorting, and delivering.

motionDna.actor: Littlebox, a closed paper box that acts through two side-seam twig arms
poses: twig arms and tiny legs carry the effort while the box stays closed
both arms bracing an external pile
deadpan dot eyes whatever happens
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image, such as the tape pressed down or the stamp landing; mini comics use two or three beats with Littlebox closed throughout

styleSheet.medium: Bold rough marker illustration with a handmade dry-brush feel
styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 on one flat pure white background (#FFFFFF) unless the user names another; Littlebox fills 35-55%
styleSheet.linework: Thick, rough black marker with dry-brush gaps and wobbly folds
avoid: an open, half-open, or cutaway box
realistic cardboard or a clean vector box icon
cute mascot, sticker, or delivery-company looks
thin, ruler-straight, or auto-traced lines
tinted, alternating, or mood-picked backgrounds the user did not ask for

legalNotice.credit: Adapted from 5km Littlebox Illustrations by okooo5km (MIT), inspected at commits 37cd93e and d760004
restrictions: Credit okooo5km or the 5km Littlebox Illustrations project in derived documentation.

sampleGates.decision: Historical examples of the pale sky-blue and lavender options, which are no longer the default: pure white is. The character source is MIT-licensed by okooo5km and credited in ATTRIBUTIONS.md.

archetypes.name: Ferris
archetypes.summary: Ferris the Rustacean, the Rust community crab, performing the idea in sparse hand-drawn article sketches without Rust logos or endorsement cues.

motionDna.actor: Ferris, who performs the central action with its claws
poses: claws, eyes, and shell angle aimed at the action
one claw clamped on a compiler gate
legs braced wide while balancing a load
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image; mini comics use two or three beats with Ferris drawn the same way in every panel

styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 on a clean white or near-white page; Ferris's action fills 35-55%
styleSheet.linework: Rough black linework with visible human looseness
avoid: Rust or Cargo logos and official badges
official Rust diagram layouts, code, and UI scenes
a generic crab or seafood icon in place of Ferris
detailed mascot rendering or polished vector style

legalNotice.credit: Ferris the Rustacean was created by Karen Rustad Tolva and dedicated to the public domain (CC0) via rustacean.net
restrictions: No claims of official Rust project affiliation or endorsement.

sampleGates.decision: Approved with trademark-safe wording when these renders were first published; Ferris is CC0, credited to Karen Rustad Tolva.

archetypes.name: Seal
archetypes.summary: A product-neutral white seal in a plain navy cap and deep-blue hoodie, always logo-free, performing the idea in sparse article sketches.

motionDna.actor: Seal, the product-neutral hoodie seal, as the central operator
poses: flippers, eyes, body, cap, hoodie, and tail turned toward the action
compact legs planted under a lift or a carry
calm, careful focus while inspecting or weighing
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image; mini comics use two or three beats with Seal consistent and active

styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 on a clean white or near-white page; Seal's action fills 35-55%
styleSheet.linework: Loose black hand-drawn lines with visible human looseness
avoid: logos, emblems, wave or cloud marks, and badges
brand or product names and endorsement cues
plush-toy or over-detailed mascot rendering
formal diagrams, UI, and code screenshots

legalNotice.credit: A product-neutral hoodie seal derived from a historical Sealos mascot image, which is not bundled
legalNotice.license: No separate character license recorded; the pack text is MIT as part of InkExplain
restrictions: Keep the seal logo-free: no cap, chest, or body logos, emblems, wave marks, or text badges.
Do not present the seal as an official Sealos mascot or as a product endorsement.

sampleGates.decision: Approved for preserved hoodie identity and logo-free output when these renders were first published.

archetypes.name: OpenClaw
archetypes.summary: The OpenClaw mascot, a red round character with claw-like arms, two antennae, and cyan pupils, performing the idea in sparse hand-drawn article sketches.

motionDna.actor: OpenClaw, the red logo mascot, as the active operator of the concept
poses: one claw grips the loose idea, thread, or key
both claw-like arms hold two parts together
the antennae lean and the cyan pupils point at the decisive object
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image; mini comics use two or three beats with all six markers in every panel

styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 on a clean white or near-white background with generous whitespace
styleSheet.linework: Loose black linework with visible hand-drawn looseness
avoid: product posters, launch graphics, and logo showcases
UI screenshots, IDE or terminal scenes, and code screenshots
formal diagrams and PPT-like infographics
over-rendered toys or logo icons

legalNotice.credit: The OpenClaw mascot comes from the OpenClaw project (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw), MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 OpenClaw Foundation, reviewed at commit c14793d
restrictions: No claims of official OpenClaw affiliation or endorsement.
No product posters, UI screenshots, terminal scenes, or code screenshots.

sampleGates.decision: Approved for logo identity, source and license review, and archetype isolation when these renders were first published; the OpenClaw project is MIT-licensed.

archetypes.name: Go Gopher
archetypes.summary: The Go gopher designed by Renee French performing the idea in sparse hand-drawn article sketches, credited and free of Go logos or endorsement claims.

motionDna.actor: The Go gopher, who performs the central action
poses: the friendly standing posture turned toward the action
a pointing paw stretched toward the useful turn
a shield stance planted in front of a fragile idea
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image; mini comics use two or three beats with the gopher identical across panels

styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 on a white or very light background; the gopher's action fills 35-55%
styleSheet.linework: Rough black outlines with visible human looseness; the gopher keeps its black outline and white sticker-like border
avoid: the Go logo and logo-forward layouts
UI, IDE, terminal, and code screenshots
language posters and mascot asset sheets
fur, 3D, or polished vector rendering

legalNotice.credit: The Go gopher was designed by Renee French (https://go.dev/blog/gopher) and is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
restrictions: Credit Renee French whenever generated images are published.
No Go logo, and no claims of official Go project affiliation, approval, sponsorship, or endorsement.

sampleGates.decision: Approved with the Renee French attribution and the CC BY 4.0 terms when these renders were first published; the credit is kept in ATTRIBUTIONS.md and next to the gallery.

archetypes.name: Tux
archetypes.summary: Tux, the Linux penguin created by Larry Ewing, performing the idea in sparse article sketches without distro logos, product graphics, or endorsement claims.

motionDna.actor: Tux, the only mascot in the frame, who performs the central action
poses: the seated, rounded body turned toward the work
a long black flipper pointing, pressing, or stamping on the object
eyes and beak aimed at the decisive point
motionDna.timing: One decisive moment per image; mini comics use two or three beats with Tux identical across panels

styleSheet.canvas: 16:9 on a white or very light background; Tux's action fills 35-55%
styleSheet.linework: Rough black hand-drawn linework with visible human looseness
avoid: distro logos, badges, and Linux Foundation logos
CLI screenshots, kernel dashboards, and product posters
generic penguin or tech-mascot rendering
gradients, shadows, and polished vector finish

legalNotice.credit: Tux was created by Larry Ewing using The GIMP (https://isc.tamu.edu/~lewing/linux/); Linux is the registered trademark of Linus Torvalds in the U.S. and other countries
legalNotice.license: Free to use and modify with credit to Larry Ewing and The GIMP when asked
restrictions: No distro logos and no Linux Foundation logos.
No claims of endorsement, certification, compatibility, affiliation, sponsorship, or approval.
No product posters, CLI screenshots, web hero graphics, kernel dashboards, or operating-system marketing graphics.

sampleGates.decision: No public samples have been reviewed yet.

identityMarkers: glossy black rounded penguin head and body
